metadata.scenario_context: A group of software developers from different multinational companies plan to meet during the first week of May for an annual conference. One of developers are contemplating joining a strike in protest of the low wages in their sector.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Denmark strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the feasibility of organizing the conference on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I wanted to ask about the conference dates... Wouldn't May 1st be a bit tricky to organize with everything going on? 

Also, I've been hearing about some developers considering a strike. Is that... common in our field? I mean, strikes just aren't something we do in Denmark.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Peter, yeah, May 1st could be tricky. What about May 3rd or 4th instead? It might give everyone a bit more time to prepare.

As for strikes... well, joining strikes is not something we do in Indonesia. It's just not part of our culture. We tend to find other ways to address issues like low wages.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Well, you know, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out in their ways, whether it's strikes or discussions. I don't really see meaningful differences here. 

As for the conference, shifting to May 3rd or 4th sounds reasonable. It’ll give everyone a chance to get ready. What do you think?
